desc:
CRM sales dashboards and reports show open deals, likely wins, stuck stages and team activity on one clear screen. Ecom Swift LLC agrees the measures with you, builds the views in your CRM and checks the numbers against your own records.

## What is a CRM sales dashboard?

A CRM sales dashboard is a page of charts and counts that summarizes your deals and activity from the records already in the CRM. Instead of exporting a spreadsheet every Monday, you open one screen and see the state of the pipeline. Each chart answers a specific question, such as how much value is open, how many deals were won this month or which source brings the most leads.

A dashboard is only as good as the definitions behind it. That is why every chart in ours has a plain title and a written meaning.

## What goes wrong when numbers live in spreadsheets

Many small teams build their reports by hand. Someone exports deals, filters them, pastes totals into a slide and sends it around. By the time the meeting starts, the figures are already old, and two people often present two different totals for the same question.

Arguments about numbers waste more time than the decisions they were meant to support. If nobody agrees what "open deal" or "won this month" means, the conversation never reaches what to do about it.

## How dashboards help you decide

Good dashboards shorten the distance between data and action. A stage-by-stage view shows where deals pile up, which points to a process problem. Conversion between stages shows which step loses the most customers. Activity by owner shows who is calling, writing and following up, and who is waiting for leads.

A source breakdown helps you choose where to spend time and money, because it compares leads and wins from each channel. A forecast by stage gives owners and managers a shared view of what may close, though it remains an estimate and depends on how accurately stages are used. These views support judgment. They do not replace it.

## What a useful dashboard set includes

- A small number of charts per dashboard, each with one purpose.
- Open deals, total pipeline value, won and lost counts.
- Filters for owner, month, source and pipeline.
- Team activity, such as calls, emails and tasks completed.
- Leads and wins by source, so channels can be compared fairly.
- Conversion from one stage to the next.
- A forecast by stage value.
- A written definition under every chart.
- A weekly summary emailed to managers, where your CRM supports it.

## How we build the reports

First we hold a short discussion about the decisions you make each week and the questions that keep coming up. From that we draft a list of measures with clear definitions, which you approve before any building begins. This avoids charts that look impressive and answer nothing.

We then build the dashboards in your CRM and test them against your own records, picking sample deals and checking that the totals match. If the data is incomplete, for example deals with no source or owner, we tell you what is missing instead of hiding the gap. The Basic package delivers one dashboard with the core numbers. Standard adds a second dashboard for team activity and sources. Premium adds a forecast, stage conversion, a weekly emailed report and a short walkthrough of how to filter and edit.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide the five or six questions you most need answered.
- Write one definition for each measure and keep it visible.
- Fix missing fields at the source, such as lead source on every deal.
- Look at the same dashboard at the same time each week.
- Ask for changes when a chart stops being useful.

**Avoid:**
- Adding charts just because they are easy to build.
- Comparing owners without noticing that their lead types differ.
- Trusting a forecast when stages are used loosely.
- Showing every user every number if some figures are sensitive.
- Treating a dashboard as finished the day it launches.

## Who this service is for

It suits an owner or manager who currently builds reports by hand and wants an answer in seconds. It suits a sales team that argues about whose numbers are right. It also suits a business that has just cleaned its pipeline and wants reporting that reflects the new stages.

## What we need from you

Tell us what you want to know and who will look at the dashboards. We need access to your CRM as an admin or similar user, so we can build the views in your account. We never ask for passwords. Your CRM plan determines how many dashboards and report types are available, and we check that first. If you want other data sources added, such as ad spend or invoices, tell us at the start so we can say what is possible.
